item.title: Bezos' Blue Origin enters the data center space race
item.description: Blue Origin, Jeff Bezos' maker of rockets and lunar landers, wants to build an orbital data center platform comprising 51,600 satellites. Others pursuing this concept include SpaceX, Google and Nvidia-backed Starcloud.

item.title: Virgin Media goes wide with 24/7 broadband support
item.description: Virgin Media has launched 24/7 support to all broadband subs at no additional cost. The operator initially rolled this out to 330,000 customers. #pressrelease

item.title: Samsung eyes death of purpose-built 5G but has no AI-RAN fears
item.description: Intel's CPUs are dislodging Marvell's custom silicon in 5G deals struck by Samsung, which is not worried about an Nvidia shakeup.

item.title: CLAR enters Japan's data center market with strategic Osaka investment
item.description: CapitaLand Ascendas REIT has acquired a 49% stake in a Tier III hyperscale facility in Osaka as part of its strategy to expand its data center portfolio in developed markets with healthy fundamentals.

item.title: Eurobites: BT plugs into £200M electricity network deal
item.description: Also in today's EMEA regional roundup: Huber+Suhner and Aurora help Vodafone update its German cable network; Iliad trumpets growth; BA's first Starlink flight takes off.

item.title: Innovative Systems scoops up Actifai
item.description: OSS and billing specialist Innovative Systems has acquired Actifai, the company behind AI-based systems for sales and customer retention and support. #pressrelease

item.title: CableLabs and Zoom team on 'Quality by Design' pilot
item.description: CableLabs and Zoom have connected on a trial to validate 'Quality by Design,' a framework that can help cable operators and application providers boost the user experience. #pressrelease

item.title: Aurora and Huber+Suhner assist Vodafone Germany on network upgrade
item.description: Aurora Networks and Huber+Suhner said they are collaborating a Vodafone Germany network upgrade that includes a distributed access network, remote PHY devices and a virtual CMTS. #pressrelease

item.title: Iliad CEO: Consolidation in France is not a matter of if, but how
item.description: Iliad CEO Thomas Reynaud says consolidation in France will happen sooner or later, while the company is also keeping a close eye on Italy following Poste Italiane's bid for Telecom Italia.

item.title: Globe Telecom conducts first live trial of direct-to-cell service
item.description: Globe Telecom has conducted its first live trial of the Starlink Mobile service in remote areas of Rizal, Batangas and Bataan in the Philippines.

item.title: A big AI upset in telecom is growing scarily possible
item.description: Rogue robots and Anthropic's warnings of disobedient technology show the risks for telcos racing to adopt agentic AI.

item.title: Eurobites: Fastweb+Vodafone is done with Inwit
item.description: Also in today's EMEA regional roundup: Openreach taps Google Cloud's AI; Noxtua clocks on at Deutsche Telekom's AI factory; Ericsson goes exascale.

item.title: The bright spot in the family budget
item.description: Data from the Bureau of Labor Statistics shows telecommunications is the largest source of consumer price relief in US household budgets. Washington must protect the framework that produced these results or risk disrupting it.

item.title: Fractus, Verizon settle patent litigation
item.description: Fractus, a company that specializes in antenna technology and IP licensing, has reached a settlement with Verizon, resolving patent infringement litigation Fractus filed in December 2024. #pressrelease

item.title: AT&T, Boldyn expand 5G subway service
item.description: AT&T and Boldyn Networks have expanded cellular service in additional tunnel segments of the MTA's 4/5 and G lines in New York City. #pressrelease
